Hildegard 0.1.11 is a pre-alpha. A computer that shares its GPU only while it's free now notices you at the keyboard
and other programs on its GPU, your takes can go to whichever of your devices is free, and the DGX Spark gets the
ComfyUI settings shared memory wants.

## Install

- **macOS and Linux:** `curl -fsSL https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.sh | sh`
- **Windows (PowerShell):** `irm https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.ps1 | iex`
- **Desktop app:** pick your system's download below, or from [dbaney.com/hildegard](https://dbaney.com/hildegard/).

Installed already? Hildegard updates itself, or run `hildegard update` (or `hildegard update all` for every device).

## New

- **Only when it's free, now with you and your other programs in view.** A computer sharing its GPU opportunistically
  (`hildegard choir opportunistic on`, or **Only when it's free** in Settings › Devices) used to go by GPU use and
  processor load alone. It now also waits while someone has used it in the last 3 minutes, and while another program
  holds a gigabyte or more of GPU memory (Linux with NVIDIA), such as a language model server waiting for requests,
  which uses no compute but leaves no room. When either shows up, a render running for another device stops within a
  few seconds and goes back in line, then starts again by itself once the computer is free. The computer stays online
  meanwhile, and Settings says why it's busy.
- **Any free device.** `hildegard choir use auto` (**Any free device** in Settings › Devices) sends each take to the
  device free for it, this one included: one with the model, that isn't busy, a device that always shares before one
  that shares only when free, then the comfortable fit and the shorter queue. A laptop in use sends its takes to the
  DGX Spark, and the other way round.
- **DGX Spark.** ComfyUI starts on the GB10 without memory-mapped weights or dynamic VRAM, which only hold each model
  twice in shared memory, and Chatterbox runs on its CPU, since that model's PyTorch has no GB10 or Arm CUDA build.
- **Omarchy.** The panel shows whether this computer shares its GPU only while it's free, and flips it. While it does,
  it tells Hildegard when you step away and come back, since Hyprland has no idle clock of its own. Other idle hooks
  can do the same with `hildegard choir presence away|back`.

Not tested on a real DGX Spark yet: if your install there doesn't find the GPU, `hildegard doctor --json` says why, and
we'd like to hear.
